title: Overnight Markets: Wall Street stumbles as health stocks fall
text:
By Himanshu Singh 31 Jan, 2018 at 02:14 
US stocks suffered a second day of steep losses on Tuesday, with the Dow registering its biggest two-day drop since September 2016, as investors dumped healthcare companies and Apple. 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 362 points, or 1.37%, to 26,077, the S&P 500 lost 31 points, or 1.09%, to 2,822 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 64 points, or 0.86%, to 7,402. 
Healthcare stocks pulled the major indexes lower on news that Amazon.com Inc (AMZN.O), Berkshire Hathaway Inc (BRKa.N) and JP Morgan Chase & Co (JPM.N) will jointly form a healthcare company to help control costs for their US employees. 
The S&P 500 Healthcare index was the day’s biggest loser among the 11 major sectors, dropping by 2.13%. 
MetLife Inc (MET.N) fell 8.6% after news the US Securities and Exchange Commission was investigating the insurer’s failure to pay some workers’ pensions. 
UnitedHealth Group Inc (UNH.N) fell 4.3%. Pfizer Inc (PFE.N) was down 3.1% despite its better-than-expected earnings and upbeat 2018 guidance. 
Harley-Davidson Inc (HOG.N) closed down 8.0% after announcing it would close a Kansas City plant in the face of declining shipments. 
Apple Inc (AAPL.O) declined for a second day, falling 0.6% on news that the US Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission are investigating the company’s disclosure that it slowed older iPhones with flagging batteries. 
US Treasury yields climbed to multi-year highs after the start of the Federal Reserve’s two-day meeting, which could shed light on the central bank’s economic and rate hike outlook. 
In Asia, most indexes traded lower on Wednesday in morning session after Wall Street sold off for a second consecutive day. 
The Nikkei 225 edged down 0.18%. Across the Korean Strait, the Kospi bucked the downward trend to climb 0.31%. Down Under, the S&P/ASX 200 edged down 0.15%. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index shed 0.06%, while on the mainland, the Shanghai composite edged down 0.26%.
